scope: Source proofreading only; no ISO build or public release.

edits.before: I-I've lost... A captain who's younger than me...
edits.after: I-I've been outdone... A captain younger than me...
edits.reason: Beecha is comparing himself with a younger captain, not reporting a battle defeat.

edits.before: Sigh... I'm... going to drag up the average age again, aren't I...?
edits.after: Sigh... I'm... going to push up the average age again, aren't I...?
edits.reason: Use a natural expression for raising the crew's average age.

edits.before: Listen, brat. We'll keep a close watch on you. Trying to escape won't do you any good, right?
edits.after: Listen, brat. We'll keep a close watch on you. Don't bother trying to escape, got it?
edits.reason: Make the guard's threat sound like a warning rather than a request for agreement.

edits.before: ...Let's wait for a chance, whether we're going to break out of here or wait for help.
edits.after: ...Let's bide our time, whether we escape on our own or wait for help.
edits.reason: Preserve both escape options while avoiding the awkward instruction to wait for a chance to wait.

edits.before: Here we are, at the hangar where Dendoh is. Let's escape, quickly.
edits.after: We've reached Dendoh's hangar. Hurry, let's get out of here.
edits.reason: Smooth Vega's urgent rescue instruction while preserving the location.

edits.before: He started suffering when he saw me...!?
edits.after: He was in pain the moment he saw me...!?
edits.reason: Express the sudden pain and Vega's surprise naturally without adding an unseen physical action.

edits.before: ...We're... in Dendoh... time to escape... buy us...
edits.after: ...We're... in Dendoh... buy us... time to escape...
edits.reason: Order the English fragments so the interrupted request is intelligible; retain all transmission gaps and the existing uncertainty.

edits.before: Are all martial artists such sweaty, overbearing men, no matter what planet they're from...?
edits.after: Are all martial artists such overbearing men, no matter what planet they're from...?
edits.reason: The insult describes an oppressive personality, not literal sweating.

edits.before: W-what are you?! What are you talking about?!
edits.after: W-who are you?! What are you talking about?!
edits.reason: Diondra is challenging Saburota's identity after his flirtatious introduction.

edits.before: Not if I can help it! Ginga and Hokuto are safe. We're getting them out of here!
edits.after: Not if I can help it! Ginga and Hokuto are safe. We're getting out of here!
edits.reason: The line announces the group's escape, not solely an extraction of the two boys.

edits.before: Unfair? Devil Saturn 6, those words suit you better than anyone!
edits.after: Unfair? Devil Saturn 6, you're hardly one to talk!
edits.reason: Render Rom's accusation of hypocrisy as an idiomatic retort.

edits.before: You two did well to keep going without giving up.
edits.after: You two did great. You never gave up.
edits.reason: Make Judau's praise sound conversational while preserving the boys' perseverance.

edits.before: No, it's thanks to everyone and Vega.
edits.after: No, we owe it to all of you and Vega.
edits.reason: Make Hokuto's humble reply natural in English.

edits.before: He's the successor to a martial art called Tenku Chushin Ken, from a planet called Cronos. I know little else about him, but...
edits.after: He's from the planet Cronos, and an heir to the martial art Tenku Chushin Ken. I know little else about him, but...
edits.reason: Attach the planetary origin clearly to Rom and preserve the martial-art lineage.

edits.before: There are also rumors... No, evidence that he has been secretly contacting remnants of the Jovian Federation.
edits.after: There are also rumors... No, there's evidence he's secretly contacting Jovian Federation remnants.
edits.reason: Repair the grammar of Meio's self-correction from rumor to evidence.

edits.before: Are you saying I must be broad-minded enough to accept both good and evil?
edits.after: Are you saying I must be willing to accept the corrupt along with the honest?
edits.reason: Render the idiom as political tolerance of honest and corrupt people, consistent with the discussion of Dorchenov.

edits.before: The Earth Sphere is now beyond saving through reforms that take their natural course.
edits.after: The Earth Sphere can no longer be saved by letting reform take its natural course.
edits.reason: Smooth Guiltorre's argument without implying that every kind of reform is futile.

edits.before: Marshal, what is the meaning of letting those young officers go without any reprimand?
edits.after: Marshal, why are those young officers being let off without so much as a reprimand?
edits.reason: Make Dorchenov's objection to leniency idiomatic.

edits.before: For the sake of Giganos's iron unity, I urge you to punish them severely!
edits.after: To preserve Giganos's ironclad unity, I urge you to punish them severely!
edits.reason: Keep the military solidarity metaphor in natural English.

edits.before: Therefore, I judge punishment unnecessary.
edits.after: I therefore consider punishment unnecessary.
edits.reason: Smooth Meio's formal judgment without weakening his position.

edits.before: And because you failed to recapture them, they have now reached the stage of producing mass-produced models.
edits.after: And because you failed to recapture them, they've now reached the mass-production stage.
edits.reason: Remove repetitive production wording while retaining the enemy's technological progress.

edits.before: Yes. Once the Federation Forces get their mass-produced Dragonars into steady production...
edits.after: Yes. Once the Federation Forces have mass production of their Dragonars running smoothly...
edits.reason: Render production getting established naturally and retain the unfinished lead-in to the predicted counteroffensive.
